description: nf-core/pathogensurveillance samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 1.1.0 nextflow_schema.json and assets/schema_input.json. Population-genomics surveillance across a set of pathogen isolates.

download_bakta_db.help: Downloads the Bakta annotation database on demand. Large; leave off unless annotation is wanted.

bakta_db.help: Path to an already-downloaded Bakta database.

n_ref_strains.help: How many reference strains to pull in per group for context.

pipeline.name: nf-core/pathogensurveillance
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample_id, name, description, path, path_2, ncbi_accession, ncbi_query, ncbi_query_max, sequence_type, report_group_ids, color_by, ploidy, enabled, ref_group_ids. The schema marks NONE strictly required, which is unusual — the pipeline accepts either local paths or NCBI accessions. NOTE sample_id/path/path_2, not sample/fastq_1/fastq_2.
pipeline.reference_requirement: NONE from us. The 1.1.0 schema declares no genome/fasta/gtf; the pipeline selects reference strains automatically from NCBI, which is what n_ref_strains controls.

validation_rules: The columns are sample_id, path and path_2 — not sample, fastq_1 and fastq_2.
sequence_type must be one of illumina, nanopore, pacbio or bgiseq. Nessie stamps it per row from the platform in the sample's metadata rather than asking; check it landed rather than assuming.
Do NOT pass --genome, --fasta or --gtf: the 1.1.0 schema declares none of them, and reference strains are chosen automatically.

report_group_ids is what makes the output useful — it defines which isolates are compared against which. It is semicolon-separated and should come from the cohort field the user actually asked about (treatment, ward, timepoint, site). A run with everything in one group produces one undifferentiated report.
This pipeline compares a SET of isolates. Running it on a single sample is valid but produces little of value.
ploidy defaults to haploid handling; set it only from real knowledge of the organism.
notes: NO MATCHING DATA IN NExtSEEK as of 2026-08-05: no bacterial isolate sequencing exists (BAC has no D.SEQ children). Catalogued for future data. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: this is the one pipeline in the batch whose value depends on a GROUPING decision rather than on the files, which puts it in the same family as differentialabundance's contrasts — Nessie knows the lineage, so it can propose the groups, and that is the interesting part.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/pathogensurveillance input sheet.

path.required: required unless an NCBI accession is given

sequence_type.description: Sequencing platform, used to pick per-sample tooling.
sequence_type.validation_hints: Derived from the sample's own platform metadata, never asked for.

report_group_ids.required: optional but the point of the pipeline
report_group_ids.description: Which comparison group(s) this isolate belongs to.
report_group_ids.validation_hints: Populate from the cohort-defining metadata the user asked about. This is the column Nessie is uniquely able to fill, because it knows the lineage.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/pathogensurveillance sheet from a resolved D.SEQ cohort of pathogen isolates.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for outbreak investigation or population-genomic comparison across isolates.
population_priority: Establish the GROUPING first — it decides what the report compares. Read the user's phrasing against the grouping_fields resolve_samples returned.
One row per D.SEQ leaf; sample_id = the UID.
Let the emitter stamp sequence_type from platform metadata.
Leave the NCBI query columns blank unless the user wants public isolates pulled in for context.
final_checks: report_group_ids is populated and reflects a real distinction, not one blanket group.
